Subject: Event history preservation questionnaire (RFP)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking the time on the RFP. Attached is our standard questionnaire (northwind_event_history_questions.xlsx) focused on event history, audit trails, data exportability, and evidence for regulatory retention. High-level asks:

- For each event type (API calls, model inference requests, user metadata changes), we need: retention windows, default and configurable retention, available export formats, and chain-of-custody guarantees.
- Export SLA expectations: timeline for bulk extracts and incremental slices; delivery mechanisms (S3 presigned, HTTPS transfer, secure FTP).
- Tamper-evidence: What manifests/signatures are provided with exported bundles?
- Redaction & PII handling: options and recommended approaches for preserving forensic value while protecting sensitive fields.

Can you route the questionnaire to the team that maintains the audit trail/export tooling and return a consolidated response by COB next Wednesday (2027-04-07)? We may follow up with a short call to clarify edge cases.

Best,
Sara Blake
Director, Procurement
Northwind Logistics

Sara —

Thanks for the questionnaire; received. I'm attaching a short capabilities summary (redwood_event_history_spec.pdf) to give a quick overview while we assemble the detailed answers.

Quick answers to the high-level asks:
- We store request-level telemetry (inference requests, API metadata, routing decisions) and system-level telemetry (scheduling, autoscale events). Retention is configurable per-account and per-route; default is 90 days for hosted plans, longer for Dedicated/Private per contract.
- Bulk extract methods: S3 transfer (customer-owned bucket with cross-account role), SFTP, or encrypted HTTPS delivery. Incremental extracts and filters supported by time range, route, and request-id.
- We produce signed delivery manifests (SHA256 checksums) for bundles and optionally timestamped signatures through our KMS integration.
- Redaction: field-level redaction, tokenization, and schema-based PII masking are available; we can provide sampling to show redaction preserves traceability.

I'll loop in Kimberly (Product Security) and Marcus (Platform) to provide the detailed per-question responses and timelines. Proposed: 30-min call next Tuesday (2027-04-06) to walk the answers and confirm any contract-level SLAs.

— Jonas
VP, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Blake <sara.blake@northwind.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Event history preservation questionnaire (RFP)

Sara —

Appended below are the detailed answers to the questionnaire you shared. I've kept item numbers aligned to the spreadsheet to make cross-referencing easier. Where helpful, I've called out default behavior, configurable options, and expected delivery times.

1) Event types captured
- Inference requests: full request payload (trimmed for large binary blobs), model variant, routing decision, latency, and token counts.
- API auth/tenant events: grant/revoke tokens, role changes, and service-account actions.
- System events: autoscaler decisions, GPU allocation/revocation, runtime restarts, and kernel-level errors.
- Audit metadata: event_id (uuid), monotonic sequence number, server_timestamp (RFC3339), customer_timestamp (if provided), and origin_host.

2) Retention windows (defaults and configurable)
- Hosted default: 90 days (rolling).
- Dedicated/Private: contractual (commonly 1, 3, or 7 years) — can be configured per-tenant and per-route.
- Granularity: retention policy can be set by event-type, route, or tag (e.g., "security-alerts" 7y, "debug-traces" 30d).

3) Export formats and schema
- Supported bundle formats: NDJSON (recommended for line-delimited event processing), Parquet (columnar, for analytics), and gzipped JSONL for compact transfer.
- Each bundle includes a top-level manifest.json (human-readable) and a signed manifest.sha256 containing checksums and the delivery signature. Example schema and a small NDJSON sample attached: redwood_ndjson-schema-example.ndjson.

4) Delivery mechanisms & SLA
- Delivery options:
  • Cross-account S3 write (preferred for large volumes).
  • HTTPS PUT to customer endpoint with mutual TLS.
  • SFTP (over SSH) with account credentials.
- SLA for prepared bulk extract (after agreement):
  • Standard: 5–7 business days to prepare and stage a full-year export (depends on dataset size).
  • Expedited: 48–72 hours for smaller slices (<500GB) if on Dedicated capacity.
- Incremental slices: support for time-windowed exports (e.g., daily/hourly) with a typical generation window of 1–4 hours for slices under 24 hours.

5) Tamper-evidence and chain of custody
- Each exported bundle includes: manifest.json, manifest.sha256, and a signature blob signed with Redwood KMS. For customers with their own HSM/KMS we can sign using customer-managed keys via our keyRotation API.
- We retain an internal audit record of each export operation (who requested, which dataset, timestamps, checksums) which is available under a separate export audit endpoint for forensic review.

6) Redaction & PII handling
- Options: schema-level redaction rules, on-export redaction (row/field-level), and pseudonymization. Redaction is parameterized by rules you define; we can perform deterministic tokenization for forensic re-identification under legal process.
- Samples: We can produce a redacted sample slice (with synthetic values replaced) for your review before full export.

7) Filtering, indexing, and searchability
- Exports can be filtered by time-range, route, event_type, request_id, and user_id. We also support exporting a separate indexed lookup table (UUID -> offset) to allow byte-range seeks into NDJSON bundles.

8) Integrity verification & validation tools
- We provide a small CLI tool (python script) and verification checksums to validate bundle integrity.
- We also provide an optional signed manifest verification flow which returns the signature verification result and a parseable errors list.

9) Forensic preservation (legal hold)
- We can place routing-level holds preventing deletion for configured windows, and generate immutable snapshots (WORM-style) on request. These snapshots are delivered as separate bundles with extended provenance metadata.

10) Escrow and long-term archives
- For very long retention (multi-year), we recommend using Dedicated/Private with periodic archive exports to customer-owned storage. We can support archival exports in industry-standard formats (Parquet + manifest) and provide retrieval tooling.

11) Pricing/tariff notes (brief)
- Exports are priced by GB prepared + egress. Expedited/forensic packaging carries a small premium. We will include a line-item estimate when you provide expected dataset size.

12) Next steps & sample deliverables
- We can produce:
  • A sample NDJSON of 10k events (redwood_ndjson-schema-example.ndjson).
  • A draft delivery manifest for your review.
  • A runbook describing export request flow and internal points of contact.

If you need more detail on any particular row in the spreadsheet, call that out and we'll prioritize. Marcus can weigh in on throughput and staging constraints if you have very large archive volumes — Marcus, can you add staging throughput guidance?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_ndjson-schema-example.ndjson (example slice), internal_export_runbook_draft.docx (internal reference)
